To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

human growth hormone (hGH) is degraded by rat hepatocytes by a process that is dependent on the binding of hGH to its receptors and is inhibited by lysosomal inhibitors and by agents that block energy-dependent processes.
degradation of cell-bound human growth hormone is receptor mediated and that it is a lysosome-dependent process.
degradation of human growth hormone in monolayer cultured hepatocytes is receptor mediated and that the receptor-bound hormone is degraded within the cell by lysosomal enzymes.

the fate of [125I]-iodo-hGH in monolayer hepatocyte cultures.
the processing of hGH in hepatocytes in vitro.
the processing of hGH by rat hepatocytes.

the fate of cell-bound hGH is degradation by an internalization-receptor-mediated process, and the degradation products are released into the extracelluar space.
the degradation of [ 125 I]iodo-hG H is a receptor-mediated, energy-requiring, lysosomotropic process.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the fate of cell-bound hGH in monolayer hepatocyte cultures is determined by the following factors: (a) the number of cell surface receptors for hGH, (b) the rate of internalization of hGH-receptor complexes, (c) the amount of lysosomal enzymes, (d) the amount of energy, and (e) the amount of extracellular space.
